column3: why was accessing specialist gender identity services in the UK difficult?

column1: I did not know where to go
My GP (General Practitioner) did not know where to refer me
My GP (General Practitioner) was not supportive
The services were not close enough to me
I had to wait too long to access the services
I wasn’t able to go at a convenient time
It was too complicated in terms of bureaucracy
Respondents could select as many options as applicable.
Only respondents who rated ease of acccess to gender identity services as 1
column2: 2 or 3 out of 5 were asked this question. Respondents who rated ease of access as 4 or 5 out of 5 have been coded as 'Did not have difficulty'.

column1: Trans people have specific health needs in relation to gender dysphoria
column2: gender reassignment or gender confirmation. These specific needs can be addressed by Gender Identity Clinics
column3: which are specialised transgender health services offered by public health services. There are eight Gender Identity Clinics in England
column5: one in Northern Ireland and none in Wales. A referral from a General Practitioner (GP) is needed to access these specialist services.
